I implicitly favored Adam at calibrated progress parity, although K1019 and K1012 explicitly warn against that tie-break. Target-dependent gradient magnitude could explain SGD’s advantage, but parameter motion was not measured. Backtesting found matched-network univariate history comparisons favoring SGD in 2/3 pairs across two questions, with one reversal. Lab parity comparisons favored SGD in only 10/33 architecture-confounded pairs across 20 univariate sets; none matched both networks. Thus neither optimizer-first rule is supported. K1002 helped place C ahead of D; the KB did not justify my mistaken D-before-B ordering.
